The correct answer is that his account of law rests on an anachronistic model of a legal system, because Austin's view of law was modelled on a historical type of legal system that has since become obsolete, so it no longer fits how modern legal systems work. (This refers to John Austin the legal philosopher, not J.L. Austin the ordinary-language philosopher, which is why my earlier answer about empiricism was off-target.)
CONFIDENCE: 80
